questions.text: भुजा l के किसी समबाहु त्रिभुज के दो शीर्षों A और B पर दो सर्वसम बिन्दु आवेश स्थित हैं । तीसरे शीर्ष P पर विद्युत क्षेत्र का परिमाण E है । यदि P पर त्रिज्या (l/4) के किसी खोखले चालक गोले को रख दिया जाए तो बिन्दु P पर विद्युत क्षेत्र का परिमाण अब होगा
questions.text_english: Two identical point charges are placed at the two vertices A and B of an equilateral triangle of side l. The magnitude of the electric field at the third vertex P is E. If a hollow conducting sphere of radius (l/4) is placed at P, the magnitude of the electric field at point P now becomes
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) E. A hollow conducting sphere placed at point P does not alter the external electric field at its centre. The charges producing the field at P are external to the sphere; a conducting sphere redistributes charge on its surface to cancel the field inside, but the field at the external point P (which is now the centre of the sphere) due to the original charges remains E. The redistribution on the sphere creates an internal cancellation, not an external one. Hence the electric field at P remains E.
questions.topic: Electric field due to point charges, conductors

questions.text: वि.वा.ब. 12 V और आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध 0.5 Ω की कोई बैटरी कुंजी से होकर किसी 9.5 Ω प्रतिरोधक से संयोजित है । बैटरी के टर्मिनलों के बीच विभवान्तरों का अनुपात, जब कुंजी खुली है और जब कुंजी बन्द है, होगा
questions.text_english: A battery of e.m.f. 12 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to a 9.5 Ω resistor through a key. The ratio of potential difference between the two terminals of the battery, when the key is open to that when the key is closed, is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1.05. When the key is open, no current flows and the terminal voltage equals the e.m.f. = 12 V. When the key is closed, current I = 12/(9.5 + 0.5) = 12/10 = 1.2 A, and terminal voltage = EMF - Ir = 12 - (1.2)(0.5) = 12 - 0.6 = 11.4 V. Ratio = 12/11.4 = 1.052 ≈ 1.05. Option (A) is correct.

questions.text: किसी प्रेरक से प्रवाहित प्रत्यावर्ती धारा I का समय t के साथ एक चक्र के प्रवाह में आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार विचरण का प्रेक्षण किया गया । नीचे दिया गया कौन सा आरेख तरंग रूप वोल्टता V का समय t के साथ सही विचरण निरूपित करता है ?
questions.text_english: The alternating current I in an inductor is observed to vary with time t as shown in the graph for a cycle. Which one of the following graphs is the correct representation of wave form of voltage V with time t?

options.A: Triangular waveform of V peaking at T/2, same shape as I but same phase
options.B: V waveform showing positive peak then going negative after T/2
options.C: V shown as a rectangular (square) pulse positive then negative
options.D: V shown as a smooth half-sine shaped positive curve

options_english.A: Triangular waveform of V peaking at T/2, in phase with I
options_english.B: V waveform positive then negative (inverted V shape with sign change)
options_english.C: V shown as rectangular positive then negative pulse
options_english.D: V shown as smooth positive half-cycle curve

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). For an inductor, V = L(dI/dt). The current I varies as a triangular wave: it increases linearly (constant positive slope) from 0 to T/2, then decreases linearly (constant negative slope) from T/2 to T. Since dI/dt is constant and positive in the first half and constant and negative in the second half, the voltage V is a rectangular (square) wave — positive constant value for 0 to T/2 and negative constant value for T/2 to T. This matches option (C).

questions.text: किसी प्रतिचुम्बकीय पदार्थ को एक-एक करके किसी छड़ चुम्बक के उत्तर ध्रुव और दक्षिण ध्रुव के निकट लाया जाता है । यह
questions.text_english: A diamagnetic substance is brought, one by one, near the north pole and the south pole of a bar magnet. It is

options.A: उत्तर ध्रुव द्वारा प्रतिकर्षित तथा दक्षिण ध्रुव द्वारा आकर्षित होता है ।
options.B: उत्तर ध्रुव द्वारा आकर्षित तथा दक्षिण ध्रुव द्वारा प्रतिकर्षित होता है ।
options.C: उत्तर ध्रुव तथा दक्षिण ध्रुव दोनों के द्वारा आकर्षित होता है ।
options.D: उत्तर ध्रुव तथा दक्षिण ध्रुव दोनों के द्वारा प्रतिकर्षित होता है ।

options_english.A: repelled by north pole and attracted by south pole.
options_english.B: attracted by north pole and repelled by south pole.
options_english.C: attracted by north pole as well as by south pole.
options_english.D: repelled by north pole as well as by south pole.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by both poles of a magnet. They develop magnetisation opposite to the applied field direction, creating a net repulsive force regardless of which pole is brought near. Unlike paramagnetic or ferromagnetic substances which are attracted, diamagnetic substances are repelled by both the north pole and the south pole of a bar magnet.

questions.text: त्रिज्या r₁ और r₂ (>r₁) को दो लम्बी परिनालिकाओं पर समाक्ष क्रमशः एक के ऊपर दूसरे के प्रति एकांक लम्बाई n₁ और n₂ फेरे लपेटे गए हैं । भीतरी परिनालिका के स्वप्रेरकत्व तथा इन दोनों परिनालिकाओं के अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व का अनुपात है –
questions.text_english: Two long solenoids of radii r₁ and r₂ (>r₁) and number of turns per unit length n₁ and n₂ respectively are co-axially wrapped one over the other. The ratio of self-inductance of inner solenoid to their mutual inductance is –
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) n₁/n₂. The self-inductance of the inner solenoid of length l is L₁ = μ₀n₁²πr₁²l. The mutual inductance between the two solenoids is M = μ₀n₁n₂πr₁²l (flux linkage is determined by the cross-sectional area of the inner solenoid since it is smaller). Therefore, L₁/M = (μ₀n₁²πr₁²l)/(μ₀n₁n₂πr₁²l) = n₁/n₂.

questions.text: किसी धारावाही चालक, जिससे x-दिशा में 1A धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है, का 1 cm लम्बा सीधा खण्ड कार्तीय निर्देशांक प्रणाली के मूलबिन्दु पर सममितः रखा है । इस खण्ड के कारण बिन्दु (1m, 1m, 0) पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र है
questions.text_english: A 1 cm straight segment of a conductor carrying 1 A current in x direction lies symmetrically at origin of Cartesian coordinate system. The magnetic field due to this segment at point (1m, 1m, 0) is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) (5.0/√2) × 10⁻¹⁰ k̂ T. Using the Biot-Savart law for a short element: dB = (μ₀/4π)(Idl sinθ/r²). Here dl = 0.01 m, I = 1 A, the point (1,1,0) is at distance r = √2 m from origin, and sinθ = sin45° = 1/√2 (angle between current direction x̂ and position vector at 45°). So dB = (10⁻⁷)(1)(0.01)(1/√2)/(√2)² = (10⁻⁷ × 0.01)/(√2 × 2) = 10⁻⁹/(2√2) = (5/√2) × 10⁻¹⁰ T. The direction by right-hand rule (x̂ × (x̂ + ŷ)/√2) = k̂ direction. Hence (C).

questions.text: किसी ac जनित्र की कुण्डली जिसमें फेरों की संख्या 100 तथा प्रत्येक फेरे का क्षेत्रफल 0.1 m² है, 0.02 T के चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में प्रति सेकण्ड आधा घूर्णन कर रही है । इस कुण्डली में उत्पन्न अधिकतम वि.वा.ब. है
questions.text_english: A coil of an ac generator, having 100 turns and area 0.1 m² each, rotates at half a rotation per second in a magnetic field of 0.02 T. The maximum emf generated in the coil is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 0.63 V. The maximum emf of an AC generator is given by E₀ = NBAω. Here N = 100, B = 0.02 T, A = 0.1 m², and the coil makes half a rotation per second so frequency f = 0.5 Hz, giving ω = 2πf = 2π × 0.5 = π rad/s. Therefore E₀ = 100 × 0.02 × 0.1 × π = 0.2π ≈ 0.2 × 3.14 ≈ 0.628 V ≈ 0.63 V.

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु की परमाणु स्पेक्ट्रमी उत्सर्जन रेखाएँ किसी जिंक पृष्ठ पर आपतन कर रही हैं । वह रेखाएँ जो इस पृष्ठ से फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों का उत्सर्जन करा सकती हैं, निम्निलिखित में से किसकी सदस्य हैं ?
questions.text_english: Atomic spectral emission lines of hydrogen atom are incident on a zinc surface. The lines which can emit photoelectrons from the surface are members of

options.D: न तो बामर, न ही पाशन और न ही लाइमैन श्रेणी

options_english.D: Neither Balmer, nor Paschen nor Lyman series

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Lyman series. The work function of zinc is approximately 4.3 eV. The Lyman series lies in the ultraviolet region with photon energies ranging from about 10.2 eV to 13.6 eV, which exceed the work function of zinc. The Balmer series lies in the visible/UV range (1.9–3.4 eV) and Paschen series in the infrared (0.66–1.9 eV), both with energies insufficient to eject photoelectrons from zinc. Therefore only Lyman series photons can cause photoelectric emission from a zinc surface.

questions.text: किसी अवतल दर्पण की वायु में फोकस दूरी f है । अपवर्तनांक 5/3 के द्रव में डुबाने पर इस दर्पण की फोकस दूरी होगी
questions.text_english: The focal length of a concave mirror in air is f. When the mirror is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 5/3, its focal length will become
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) f. The focal length of a mirror depends only on its radius of curvature (f = R/2) and is independent of the medium in which it is placed. Unlike lenses, mirrors work by reflection and not refraction, so the refractive index of the surrounding medium does not affect their focal length. Therefore, when the concave mirror is immersed in a liquid, its focal length remains f.
questions.topic: Mirror formula, focal length and medium

options.A: संरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश नहीं बनाती हैं ।
options.B: संरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश बनाती हैं ।
options.C: असंरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश नहीं बनाती हैं ।
options.D: असंरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश बनाती हैं ।

options_english.A: conservative and field lines do not form closed loops.
options_english.B: conservative and field lines form closed loops.
options_english.C: non-conservative and field lines do not form closed loops.
options_english.D: non-conservative and field lines form closed loops.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). The electric field due to static charges is conservative in nature, meaning the work done in moving a charge around a closed path is zero. Electric field lines start from positive charges and end on negative charges; they never form closed loops. Closed loops are a property of magnetic field lines. Options (B), (C), and (D) are incorrect because the field is conservative and its lines do not form closed loops.

questions.text: जब किसी p-n संधि डायोड के p और n सिरों के बीच मापित प्रतिरोध उच्च होता है, तब यह निम्निलिखित में से किसकी भाँति कार्य कर सकता है ?
questions.text_english: When the resistance measured between p and n ends of a p-n junction diode is high, it can act as a/an –
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) switch. A p-n junction diode has very high resistance when reverse biased (open switch condition) and very low resistance when forward biased (closed switch condition). When the measured resistance is high, the diode is in reverse bias and behaves like an open switch — effectively no current flows. This switching behaviour is the fundamental operating principle of diodes in digital circuits.

questions.text: किसी हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन की निम्नतम अवस्था में ऊर्जा –13.6 eV है । क्वान्टम संख्या n के तद्नुरूप किसी कक्षा में इसकी ऊर्जा –0.544 eV है । n का मान है
questions.text_english: The energy of an electron in a hydrogen atom in ground state is –13.6 eV. Its energy in an orbit corresponding to quantum number n is –0.544 eV. The value of n is
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 5. The energy of an electron in the nth orbit is given by Eₙ = E₁/n² = -13.6/n² eV. Setting -13.6/n² = -0.544, we get n² = 13.6/0.544 = 25, so n = 5. Therefore the quantum number is 5.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : अवरक्त तरंगों और रेडियो तरंगों में से रेडियो तरंगें विस्तृत विवर्तन प्रभाव दर्शा सकती हैं ।
कारण (R) : अवरक्त तरंगों की तुलना में रेडियो तरंगों की आवृत्ति अधिक होती है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Out of Infrared and radio waves, the radio waves show more diffraction effect.
Reason (R) : Radio waves have greater frequency than infrared waves.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 के लिए, दो कथन दिए गए हैं – जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है । इन प्रश्नों के सही उत्तर नीचे दिए गए कोडों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से चुनकर दीजिए ।
questions.instruction_line_english: For Questions 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled Assertion (A) and other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं ।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion is true: radio waves have much longer wavelengths than infrared waves (radio waves: metres to kilometres; infrared: micrometres), and since diffraction is more pronounced when wavelength is comparable to or larger than the obstacle/slit size, radio waves show greater diffraction. However, the Reason is false: radio waves actually have lower frequency than infrared waves (frequency is inversely proportional to wavelength). The reason for more diffraction in radio waves is their greater wavelength, not greater frequency.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : किसी आदर्श अपचायी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में विद्युत ऊर्जा का क्षय नहीं होता है ।
कारण (R) : किसी अपचायी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में वोल्टता घटती है, परन्तु धारा बढ़ती है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In an ideal step-down transformer, the electrical energy is not lost.
Reason (R) : In a step-down transformer, voltage decreases but the current increases.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं ।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, but the Reason does not correctly explain the Assertion. The Assertion is true: in an ideal transformer there are no energy losses (no copper loss, no iron loss, no flux leakage). The Reason is also true: in a step-down transformer, voltage decreases and current increases proportionally so that power (P = VI) remains constant. However, the reason that energy is not lost is not because voltage decreases and current increases — that is simply the transformation ratio. Energy is conserved because the transformer is ideal. Hence (B).

अभिकथन (A) : हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में nवीं कक्षा के इलेक्ट्रॉन का कोणीय संवेग उसकी कक्षा की त्रिज्या rₙ के वर्गमूल के अनुपाती होता है ।

Assertion (A) : In Bohr model of hydrogen atom, the angular momentum of an electron in nth orbit is proportional to the square root of its orbit radius rₙ.
Reason (R) : According to Bohr model, electron can jump to its nearest orbits only.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं ।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion is true: in the Bohr model, angular momentum L = nh/2π = nℏ, and orbital radius rₙ = n²a₀, so n ∝ √rₙ, meaning L ∝ √rₙ. The Reason is false: according to Bohr's model, an electron can jump between any two allowed orbits, not just nearest ones. There is no restriction to adjacent orbits; transitions can occur between any two energy levels.
questions.topic: Bohr model, angular momentum, orbital radius

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : किसी अर्धचालक डायोड में ह्रासी स्तर की मोटाई अचर नहीं होती है ।
कारण (R) : अर्धचालक युक्तियों में ह्रासी स्तर की मोटाई बहुत से कारकों, जैसे अर्धचालक के बायसन पर निर्भर करती है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In a semiconductor diode the thickness of depletion layer is not fixed.
Reason (R) : Thickness of depletion layer in a semiconductor device depends upon many factors such as biasing of the semiconductor.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं ।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. The depletion layer in a p-n junction diode is not fixed in thickness — it varies depending on the biasing conditions. Under forward bias, the depletion layer narrows, and under reverse bias it widens. This variation in thickness is directly because the depletion layer depends on factors such as the type and degree of biasing applied to the semiconductor, as correctly stated in the Reason.

questions.text: सिलिकॉन डायोड की देहली वोल्टता 0.7 V है । इस बिन्दु पर V वोल्ट की किसी बैटरी के साथ श्रेणी में डायोड और 1000 Ω के किसी प्रतिरोधक को संयोजित करके इसे प्रचालित किया गया है । उस स्थिति में V का मान ज्ञात कीजिए जब ली गयी धारा 15 mA है ।
questions.text_english: The threshold voltage of a silicon diode is 0.7 V. It is operated at this point by connecting the diode in series with a battery of V volt and a resistor of 1000 Ω. Find the value of V when the current drawn is 15 mA.

key_points: Apply Kirchhoff's voltage law: V = V_diode + V_resistor

questions.solution: Using Kirchhoff's voltage law around the circuit: the applied voltage V equals the voltage drop across the diode plus the voltage drop across the resistor. The diode operates at its threshold voltage of 0.7 V. The voltage across the 1000 Ω resistor when current I = 15 mA = 15 × 10⁻³ A is V_R = IR = 15 × 10⁻³ × 1000 = 15 V. Therefore, V = 0.7 + 15 = 15.7 V.

questions.text: हाइगेन्स सिद्धान्त का उपयोग करके किसी समतल अन्तरापृष्ठ पर प्रकाश तरंग का अपवर्तन दर्शाइए तथा स्नेल के नियम का सत्यापन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Show the refraction of light wave at a plane interface using Huygens' principle and prove Snell's law.

key_points: Draw incident wavefront AB reaching interface; secondary wavelets drawn from A
Time for wavefront to travel BC in medium 1 equals time for secondary wavelet from A to reach D in medium 2
BC = v₁t and AD = v₂t; using geometry sin i = BC/AC and sin r = AD/AC
Therefore sin i/sin r = v₁/v₂ = n₂/n₁ which is Snell's law

questions.solution: Consider a plane wavefront AB incident on a plane interface between medium 1 (speed v₁) and medium 2 (speed v₂). When point A of the wavefront touches the interface, point B is still at distance BC from it. Let t be the time for B to reach C. In this time t, the secondary wavelet from A travels a distance AD = v₂t in medium 2, while BC = v₁t in medium 1. The refracted wavefront is CD, tangent to the secondary wavelet from A. From geometry: sin i = BC/AC = v₁t/AC and sin r = AD/AC = v₂t/AC. Dividing: sin i/sin r = v₁/v₂ = n₂/n₁, which is Snell's law (n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r).

questions.text: दो उत्तल लेंसों A और B जिनमें प्रत्येक की फोकस दूरी 10 cm है, को किसी प्रकाशिक बेन्च पर क्रमशः 50.0 cm और 70.0 cm पर आरोपित किया गया है । किसी बिम्ब को इस बेन्च पर 20.0 cm पर आरोपित किया गया है । लेंसों के संयोजन द्वारा बने अंतिम प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति और स्थिति ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Two convex lenses A and B, each of focal length 10.0 cm, are mounted on an optical bench at 50.0 cm and 70.0 cm respectively. An object is mounted at 20.0 cm. Find the nature and position of the final image formed by the combination.

key_points: Object distance for lens A: u₁ = 20 - 50 = -30 cm; using 1/v - 1/u = 1/f: 1/v₁ = 1/10 + 1/(-30) gives v₁ = 15 cm, image at 50+15 = 65 cm
Final image is virtual, erect, at 70 - 10 = 60 cm on the bench

questions.solution: For lens A (at 50 cm), the object is at 20 cm, so u₁ = 20 - 50 = -30 cm and f = 10 cm. Using 1/v - 1/u = 1/f: 1/v₁ = 1/10 - 1/30 = 3/30 - 1/30 = 2/30, so v₁ = 15 cm to the right of lens A, i.e., at 65 cm on the bench. For lens B (at 70 cm), u₂ = 65 - 70 = -5 cm and f = 10 cm. 1/v₂ = 1/10 - 1/5 = 1/10 - 2/10 = -1/10, so v₂ = -10 cm. The final image is 10 cm to the left of lens B, i.e., at 60 cm on the bench. The image is virtual and erect.

questions.text: कार्य फलन 2.0 eV के किसी धातु के पृष्ठ पर दो विभिन्न आवृत्तियों के विकिरणों को एक-एक करके आपतित कराया गया है । इनके फोटॉनों की ऊर्जाएँ क्रमशः 2.5 eV और 4.5 eV हैं । दोनों प्रकरणों में उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम चालों का अनुपात ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Radiations of two frequencies are incident on a metal surface of work function 2.0 eV one by one. The energies of their photons are 2.5 eV and 4.5 eV respectively. Find the ratio of the maximum speed of the electrons emitted in the two cases.

key_points: KE = ½mv² so v ∝ √KE

questions.solution: Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, maximum kinetic energy = photon energy - work function. For the first radiation: KE₁ = 2.5 - 2.0 = 0.5 eV. For the second radiation: KE₂ = 4.5 - 2.0 = 2.5 eV. Since KE = ½mv², the maximum speed v is proportional to √KE. Therefore, v₁/v₂ = √(KE₁/KE₂) = √(0.5/2.5) = √(1/5) = 1/√5. The ratio of maximum speeds is 1 : √5.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photoelectric effect, maximum speed of electrons

questions.text_english:
(a) Two wires of the same material and the same radius have their lengths in the ratio 2 : 3. They are connected in parallel to a battery which supplies a current of 15 A. Find the current through the wires.
OR
(b) In the circuit three ideal cells of e.m.f. V, V and 2V are connected to a resistor of resistance R, a capacitor of capacitance C and another resistor of resistance 2R as shown in figure. In the steady state find (i) the potential difference between P and Q and (ii) potential difference across capacitor C.

key_points: (a) Resistance ∝ length (same material, same radius); R₁:R₂ = 2:3; currents in parallel inversely proportional to resistance; I₁:I₂ = 3:2; I₁ = 9A, I₂ = 6A
(b) In steady state no current through capacitor branch; net EMF in outer loop = V + 2V - V = 2V through R and 2R; I = 2V/3R; V_PQ = 4V/3; V_C = V

questions.solution:
Part (a): Since both wires are of the same material and same radius, their resistance is proportional to their length. So R₁ : R₂ = 2 : 3. In a parallel connection, current is inversely proportional to resistance, so I₁ : I₂ = 3 : 2. Total current = 15 A, so I₁ = (3/5) × 15 = 9 A and I₂ = (2/5) × 15 = 6 A.

Part (b): In steady state, no current flows through the capacitor branch. Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law to the outer loop containing EMFs V, 2V and V with resistors R and 2R: net EMF = V + 2V - V = 2V (taking direction carefully). Current I = 2V/(R + 2R) = 2V/3R. Potential difference V_PQ = EMF of middle branch = V (voltage across the capacitor branch equals the EMF of the cell V in that branch in steady state, as no current flows through it). The voltage across capacitor C = V.
questions.topic: Parallel resistors, Kirchhoff's laws, capacitor in steady state

(b) (i) "किसी निम्न वोल्टता की बैटरी, जिससे उच्च धारा चाहिए, का आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध निम्न होना चाहिए ।" पुष्टि कीजिए ।

questions.text_english:
(a) Define resistivity of a conductor. Discuss its dependence on temperature of the conductor and draw a plot of resistivity of copper as a function of temperature.
(b) (i) "A low voltage battery from which high current is required must have low internal resistance." Justify.
    (ii) "A high voltage battery must have a large internal resistance." Justify.

key_points: Resistivity ρ = RA/l; it is property of material independent of shape/size
For metals: ρ increases linearly with temperature (ρ = ρ₀(1 + αT)); copper graph shows linear increase
(i) Terminal voltage V = EMF - Ir; for high current from low EMF, internal resistance r must be low to minimize voltage drop
(ii) High voltage battery: if r is small and accidentally short-circuited, enormous current flows causing damage; large r limits short-circuit current

questions.solution: Resistivity (ρ) of a conductor is defined as the resistance offered by a conductor of unit length and unit cross-sectional area. It is given by ρ = RA/l, where R is resistance, A is cross-sectional area and l is length. Resistivity is a property of the material and does not depend on the shape or size of the conductor. For metals like copper, resistivity increases nearly linearly with temperature: ρ = ρ₀(1 + αT), where α is the temperature coefficient. The graph of copper's resistivity vs temperature is a straight line with a positive slope starting from a small non-zero value at 0 K. For part (b)(i): The current from a battery is I = EMF/(R + r). For a low-voltage battery to supply high current, the denominator (R + r) must be small. Since the external resistance R is determined by the load, the internal resistance r must be as small as possible to avoid significant voltage drop inside the battery itself. For part (b)(ii): A high-voltage battery with low internal resistance could deliver dangerously large short-circuit currents if accidentally connected to a low resistance circuit. A large internal resistance limits this current to a safe value and protects the circuit.

questions.text_english:
(a) When a parallel beam of light enters water surface obliquely at some angle, what is the effect on the width of the beam?
(b) With the help of a ray diagram, show that a straw appears bent when it is partly dipped in water and explain it.
(c) Explain the transmission of optical signal through an optical fibre by a diagram.

key_points: (a) Width of beam decreases when entering denser medium obliquely due to refraction bending rays closer together
(b) Ray diagram showing straw appearing bent at water surface; light from submerged part bends away from normal at interface, making it appear shifted
(c) Optical fibre uses total internal reflection; light undergoes repeated TIR at core-cladding interface and travels long distances

questions.solution: Part (a): When a parallel beam of light enters a denser medium (water) obliquely, each ray bends towards the normal at the interface. As a result, the rays come closer together, and the width (thickness) of the beam decreases after entering water. Part (b): A ray from the submerged portion of the straw travels in water and hits the water-air interface. Since it travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal. To an observer above the water, the ray appears to come from a higher and shifted position, making the submerged part of the straw appear bent at the surface. Part (c): An optical fibre consists of a dense core surrounded by a less dense cladding. Light entering at one end strikes the core-cladding boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle, undergoes total internal reflection, and bounces along the fibre without escaping. This repeated total internal reflection allows optical signals to be transmitted over long distances with minimal loss.
questions.topic: Refraction, apparent bending, total internal reflection, optical fibre

questions.text: किसी प्रत्यावर्ती धारा (ac) के शिखर मान तथा वर्ग माध्य मूल मान के बीच अन्तर लिखिए । शिखर मान के पदों में प्रत्यावर्ती धारा के वर्ग माध्य मूल मान के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Differentiate between the peak value and root mean square value of an alternating current. Derive the expression for the root mean square value of alternating current, in terms of its peak value.

key_points: Peak value I₀ is maximum current; RMS value I_rms is the DC equivalent that produces same heating effect
I = I₀ sin(ωt); I² = I₀² sin²(ωt)
Mean of I² over full cycle = I₀²/2; I_rms = I₀/√2 ≈ 0.707 I₀

questions.solution: The peak value (I₀) of an alternating current is the maximum value attained during a cycle. The root mean square (RMS) value (I_rms) is the value of DC current that would produce the same heating effect as the alternating current; it represents the effective value of the AC. To derive: Let I = I₀ sin(ωt). The mean square value over one complete cycle is: <I²> = (1/T) ∫₀ᵀ I₀² sin²(ωt) dt = I₀²/2, since the mean value of sin²(ωt) over a complete cycle is 1/2. Therefore, I_rms = √(<I²>) = √(I₀²/2) = I₀/√2. The RMS value of an alternating current is I₀/√2, which is approximately 0.707 times the peak value.
questions.topic: Peak value, RMS value of AC

questions.text_english:
(a) How is an electromagnetic wave produced?
(b) An electromagnetic wave is travelling in vertically upward direction. At an instant, its electric field vector points in west direction. In which direction does the magnetic field vector point at that instant?
(c) Estimate the ratio of shortest wave length of radio waves to the longest wave length of gamma waves.

key_points: (a) EM waves produced by accelerating charges; oscillating electric and magnetic fields regenerate each other
(b) Using E × B = direction of propagation; propagation upward (+z), E westward (-x); B must be southward (-y) since (-x) × (-y) = +z
(c) Shortest radio wavelength ≈ 0.1 m; longest gamma wavelength ≈ 10⁻¹⁰ m; ratio ≈ 0.1/10⁻¹⁰ = 10⁹

questions.solution: Part (a): Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating or oscillating electric charges. An oscillating charge creates an oscillating electric field which in turn produces an oscillating magnetic field; these mutually perpendicular oscillating fields propagate outward as an electromagnetic wave, carrying energy through space. Part (b): The direction of propagation of an EM wave is given by E × B. The wave travels vertically upward (+z direction) and E points west (-x direction). Using the right-hand rule, if E is in -x and we need E × B = +z, then B must point in the -y direction (south). So the magnetic field vector points towards the south at that instant. Part (c): The shortest wavelength of radio waves is approximately 0.1 m (= 10⁻¹ m), and the longest wavelength of gamma rays is approximately 10⁻¹⁰ m. The ratio = (10⁻¹)/(10⁻¹⁰) = 10⁹.
questions.topic: Production of EM waves, direction of fields, EM spectrum

questions.text:
(a) एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र E→ के प्रदेश में XX' अक्ष के संपाती किसी धारावाही लम्बे सीधे चालक जिससे -X अक्ष की ओर धारा I प्रवाहित हो रही है, के निकट कोई ऋणावेशित कण किसी नियत वेग v→ = -v₀î से गतिमान है । यह कण चालक से दूरी d पर रहता है ।
(i) विद्युत क्षेत्र और चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशाओं को दर्शाने वाला आरेख खींचिए ।
(ii) आवेशित कण पर लगने वाले विभिन्न बलों का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
(iii) E, d और I के पदों में v₀ का मान ज्ञात कीजिए ।
अथवा
(b) XX' और YY' अक्षों के अनुदिश रखे दो अनन्त लम्बाई के चालकों से I₁ और I₂ धाराएँ क्रमशः -X अक्ष और -Y अक्ष के अनुदिश प्रवाहित हो रही हैं । बिन्दु P(X, Y) पर उत्पन्न नेट चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र का परिमाण और दिशा ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) In a region of a uniform electric field E→, a negatively charged particle is moving with a constant velocity v→ = -v₀î near a long straight conductor coinciding with XX' axis and carrying current I towards -X axis. The particle remains at a distance d from the conductor.
(i) Draw diagram showing direction of electric and magnetic fields.
(ii) What are the various forces acting on the charged particle?
(iii) Find the value of v₀ in terms of E, d and I.
OR
(b) Two infinitely long conductors kept along XX' and YY' axes are carrying current I₁ and I₂ along -X axis and -Y axis respectively. Find the magnitude and direction of the net magnetic field produced at point P(X, Y).

key_points: (a)(i) Current along -X; by right-hand rule, B at particle location points upward (+z or +k); E is given (uniform, assume along some direction)
(a)(ii) Forces: electric force qE (upward for negative charge if E downward), magnetic force qv×B, and gravity
(a)(iii) For constant velocity, net force = 0; electric and magnetic forces balance; magnetic field B = μ₀I/(2πd); eE = ev₀B gives v₀ = 2πdE/(μ₀I)
(b) B₁ = μ₀I₁/(2πY) (-k̂) and B₂ = μ₀I₂/(2πX) (+k̂); net B magnitude and direction by superposition

questions.solution:
Part (a): The current flows in the -X direction. By the right-hand rule (or Ampere's law), the magnetic field at a point below the wire (at distance d in the -Y direction) points in the -Z direction (into the page). The uniform electric field E→ is given externally. Part (ii): The forces on the negatively charged particle are: (1) Electric force F_E = qE (since charge is negative, force is opposite to E); (2) Magnetic force F_B = qv × B (Lorentz force); (3) Gravitational force mg downward (often neglected). For constant velocity, the net force must be zero. Part (iii): The magnetic field due to the current-carrying wire at distance d is B = μ₀I/(2πd). For equilibrium, the electric force must balance the magnetic force: qE = qv₀B, giving v₀ = E/B = E × 2πd/(μ₀I) = 2πdE/(μ₀I).

Part (b): The conductor along XX' carries current I₁ in the -X direction. At point P(X, Y), its distance from the XX' axis is Y. The magnetic field due to this conductor at P is B₁ = μ₀I₁/(2πY) directed in the -k̂ direction (into page). The conductor along YY' carries current I₂ in the -Y direction. At point P(X, Y), its distance from the YY' axis is X. The magnetic field due to this conductor at P is B₂ = μ₀I₂/(2πX) directed in the +k̂ direction (out of page). The net magnetic field B_net = B₂ - B₁ = (μ₀/2π)[I₂/X - I₁/Y] k̂ in magnitude and direction.
questions.topic: Magnetic force on charged particle, Ampere's law

questions.text:
(a) किसी अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक में बहुसंख्यक और अल्पसंख्यक आवेश वाहक क्या होते हैं ?

questions.text_english:
(a) What are majority and minority charge carriers in an extrinsic semiconductor?
(b) A p-n junction is forward biased. Describe the movement of the charge carriers which produce current in it.
(c) The graph shows the variation of current with voltage for a p-n junction diode. Estimate the dynamic resistance of diode at V = -0.6 volt.

key_points: (a) In n-type: majority = electrons, minority = holes; in p-type: majority = holes, minority = electrons
(b) In forward bias: holes in p-region move towards junction, electrons in n-region move towards junction; they recombine at junction, maintaining current
(c) Dynamic resistance r = ΔV/ΔI; at V=-0.6V in reverse bias, from graph ΔV ≈ 0.6V corresponds to ΔI ≈ 1μA (nearly constant); r = 0.6V/1×10⁻⁶A = 6×10⁵ Ω

questions.solution: Part (a): In an extrinsic (doped) semiconductor, majority carriers are those present in large numbers due to doping — electrons in n-type and holes in p-type. Minority carriers are thermally generated and present in small numbers — holes in n-type and electrons in p-type. Part (b): When a p-n junction is forward biased, the positive terminal of the battery is connected to the p-side and the negative to the n-side. This reduces the depletion layer. Holes in the p-region are pushed towards the junction, and electrons in the n-region are pushed towards the junction. At the junction, electrons and holes recombine. This recombination is continuously compensated by electrons injected from the battery into the n-side and holes created at the p-side, thus maintaining a continuous current. Part (c): At V = -0.6 V (reverse bias region), from the graph the current is nearly constant (approximately 1 μA ≈ 10⁻³ mA). For a small change ΔV = 0.2 V (between -0.4 V and -0.6 V), ΔI ≈ 0 (virtually unchanged). Dynamic resistance r_d = ΔV/ΔI. From the graph, in the reverse bias region near -0.6 V, ΔV ≈ 0.6 V and ΔI ≈ 10⁻³ mA = 10⁻⁶ A, giving r_d = 0.6/10⁻⁶ = 6 × 10⁵ Ω.

questions.text_english:
(a) Show the variation of binding energy per nucleon with mass number. Write the significance of the binding energy curve.
(b) Two nuclei with lower binding energy per nucleon form a nuclei with more binding energy per nucleon.
(i) What type of nuclear reaction is it?
(ii) Whether the total mass of nuclei increases, decreases or remains unchanged?
(iii) Does the process require energy or produce energy?

key_points: (a) Curve: rises steeply for light nuclei, peak ~8.7 MeV/nucleon at Fe-56, gradually decreases for heavy nuclei; significance: fusion possible for light nuclei, fission possible for heavy nuclei
(b)(i) Nuclear fusion
(b)(ii) Total mass decreases (mass defect converted to energy)
(b)(iii) Energy is produced (released)

questions.solution: Part (a): The binding energy per nucleon curve starts low for very light nuclei (like hydrogen), rises steeply for light nuclei, reaches a peak of about 8.7 MeV/nucleon around mass number A = 56 (iron region), and then gradually decreases for heavier nuclei. Significance: Nuclei near the peak (iron group) are the most stable. For nuclei lighter than iron, fusion of lighter nuclei into heavier ones releases energy. For nuclei heavier than iron, fission into lighter fragments releases energy. This explains both nuclear fusion in stars and nuclear fission in reactors. Part (b)(i): When two light nuclei with low binding energy per nucleon combine to form a heavier nucleus with higher binding energy per nucleon, this is a nuclear fusion reaction. Part (b)(ii): The total mass of the nuclei decreases. The product nucleus has less mass than the sum of masses of the combining nuclei; this mass defect (Δm) is converted to energy. Part (b)(iii): Energy is produced (released) in the process. The energy released is given by E = Δmc², which is the binding energy difference between the products and the reactants.
questions.topic: Binding energy per nucleon, nuclear fusion

questions.text: जब कोई उचित आवृत्ति का फोटॉन किसी धातु के पृष्ठ पर आपतन करता है, तो उससे कोई फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित होता है । यदि यह आवृत्ति पृष्ठ की देहली आवृत्ति (v₀) से कम होती है तो फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों का उत्सर्जन नहीं होता है । फोटॉन की किसी आवृत्ति v(v > v₀) के लिए उत्सर्जित फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों की गतिज ऊर्जा h(v – v₀) होती है । एनोड पर किसी विभव V₀, जिसे निरोधी विभव कहते हैं, का अनुप्रयोग करके प्रकाशिक धारा को रोका जा सकता है । इस प्रकार फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा K_m = eV₀ = h(v – v₀) । आरेख में किसी धातु के लिए V₀ और v के बीच प्रायोगिक ग्राफ दर्शाया गया है । यह सरल रेखा है जिसकी प्रवणता (ढाल) m है ।
questions.text_english: When a photon of suitable frequency is incident on a metal surface, photoelectron is emitted from it. If the frequency is below a threshold frequency (v₀) for the surface, no photoelectron is emitted. For a photon of frequency v(v > v₀), the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is h(v – v₀). The photocurrent can be stopped by applying a potential V₀ called 'stopping potential' on the anode. Thus maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons K_m = eV₀ = h(v – v₀). The experimental graph between V₀ and v for a metal is shown in figure. This is a straight line of slope m.

sub_questions.solution: The slope of the V₀ vs v graph is m = h/e (Planck's constant divided by electron charge), which is a universal constant independent of the metal. Different metals have different threshold frequencies v₀ (different work functions), which shift the x-intercept of the graph. Since all metals give the same slope but different x-intercepts, the lines are parallel to each other.

sub_questions.text: इस धातु के लिए प्लांक नियतांक का मान है –
sub_questions.text_english: The value of Planck's constant for this metal is
sub_questions.solution: From eV₀ = h(v – v₀), we get V₀ = (h/e)v – (hv₀/e). The slope of the V₀ vs v graph is h/e = m. Therefore, Planck's constant h = me, i.e., h = m × e. So the value of Planck's constant is m/e... wait: slope m = h/e, so h = me. Option (C) me is correct.

sub_questions.text: ग्राफ के v-अक्ष और V₀-अक्ष के कटान हैं क्रमशः :
sub_questions.text_english: The intercepts on v-axis and V₀-axis of the graph are respectively :
sub_questions.solution: From the equation V₀ = (h/e)(v – v₀): when V₀ = 0, v = v₀, so the v-axis intercept is v₀ (threshold frequency). When v = 0, V₀ = –hv₀/e, meaning the V₀-axis intercept (where graph meets V₀ axis by extrapolation) is –hv₀/e. The magnitude of the V₀-axis intercept is hv₀/e. Therefore the intercepts are v₀ and hv₀/e respectively, which is option (A).

sub_questions.text: जब किसी फोटॉन की तरंगदैर्घ्य दो गुनी की जाती है तो उसकी तरंग संख्या और आवृत्ति क्रमशः कितने गुनी हो जाती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: When the wavelength of a photon is doubled, how many times its wave number and frequency become, respectively?
sub_questions.solution: Wave number k = 1/λ (or 2π/λ) and frequency v = c/λ. When wavelength λ is doubled (λ → 2λ), wave number k = 1/λ becomes 1/(2λ) = k/2, so wave number becomes half (1/2 times). Similarly, frequency v = c/λ becomes c/(2λ) = v/2, so frequency also becomes half (1/2 times). Hence both wave number and frequency become 1/2 times, which is option (B).

This electric field between the two plates depends upon the potential difference applied, the separation of the plates and nature of the medium between the plates.

sub_questions.text: किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र की पट्टिकाओं के बीच विद्युत क्षेत्र E है । अब पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन को दो गुना तथा साथ ही पट्टिकाओं के बीच प्रयुक्त विभवान्तर को मूल विभवान्तर का आधा कर दिया गया है । पट्टिकाओं के बीच नया विद्युत क्षेत्र होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: The electric field between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor is E. Now the separation between the plates is doubled and simultaneously the applied potential difference between the plates is reduced to half of its initial value. The new value of the electric field between the plates will be:
sub_questions.solution: The electric field between parallel plates is E = V/d. Initially E = V/d. Now V becomes V/2 and d becomes 2d. New electric field E' = (V/2)/(2d) = V/(4d) = E/4. So the new electric field is E/4, option (C).

sub_questions.text: किसी संधारित्र, जिसकी पट्टिकाओं का पृथकन d समय के साथ विचरण करता है, की पट्टिकाओं के बीच नियत विद्युत क्षेत्र बनाए रखना है । नियत विद्युत क्षेत्र बनाए रखने के लिए निम्निलिखित में से कौन सा एक ग्राफ पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन (d) को फलन के रूप में लेकर पट्टिकाओं के बीच अनुप्रयुक्त की जाने वाली वोल्टता (V) का सही चित्रण करता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: A constant electric field is to be maintained between the two plates of a capacitor whose separation d changes with time. Which of the graphs correctly depict the potential difference (V) to be applied between the plates as a function of separation between the plates (d) to maintain the constant electric field?

options.A: Concave curve (V increases rapidly with d)

options_english.D: Straight line through origin (V proportional to d)

sub_questions.solution: To maintain constant electric field E = V/d = constant, we need V = E × d. Since E is constant, V is directly proportional to d: V ∝ d. This is a linear relationship — V vs d is a straight line through the origin, which corresponds to option (D).

sub_questions.text: ऊपर दिए गए आरेख में P और Q किसी संधारित्र की दो समान्तर पट्टिकाएँ हैं । पट्टिका Q पट्टिका P के सापेक्ष धनात्मक विभव पर है । MN दोनों पट्टिकाओं के लम्बवत् खींची गयी काल्पनिक रेखा है । कौन सा ग्राफ रेखा MN के अनुदिश विद्युत क्षेत्र तीव्रता E के परिमाण के विचरण को सही दर्शाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: In the above figure P, Q are the two parallel plates of a capacitor. Plate Q is at positive potential with respect to plate P. MN is an imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the plates. Which of the graphs shows correctly the variations of the magnitude of electric field strength E along the line MN?

options.C: Flat line (constant E between plates, zero outside)
options.D: Peaks at edges, dips in middle

options_english.C: Constant E between plates and zero outside

sub_questions.solution: For an ideal parallel plate capacitor, the electric field exists only between the plates and is uniform (constant magnitude E = σ/ε₀). Outside the plates, the field is zero (fields from the two oppositely charged plates cancel). So along line MN: E = 0 from M to the first plate, E = constant between the plates, and E = 0 from the second plate to N. This flat-topped rectangular graph is option (C).

31(a)(ii): Angle of prism A=30°, deviation δ=15°, i₁=45°; by geometry r₁+r₂=A=30°; i₂=0° (normal emergence); r₂=0, r₁=30°; n=sin45°/sin30°=√2
31(b)(i)(2): Coincidence when n₁λ₁=n₂λ₂; n₁/n₂=480/600=4/5; min n₁=4,n₂=5; y=4×600nm×1m/1mm=2.4mm
31(b)(ii)(1): Single slit minima at sin θ = nλ/a; graph shows central maximum flanked by secondary maxima of decreasing intensity

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): Let the tip of the pencil be at the centre of curvature C (distance 2f from mirror). The base of the pencil is at distance 2f + f/4 = 9f/4 from the mirror. For the tip at u = -2f: using mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/f - 1/(-2f) gives v = -2f (real image at C, same position). For the base at u = -9f/4: 1/v = 1/f + 1/(9f/4) → 1/v = (9-4)/(9f/4)... The image just touches the pencil, meaning the image of the near end of the pencil coincides with the pencil's near end. Using the mirror formula for the far end (at 2f + f/4) gives the image between C and the pencil. The magnification m = -v/u = -(–3f)/(–f) gives magnification of 3.

Part (a)(ii): Angle of prism A = 30°, angle of incidence i₁ = 45°, deviation δ = 15°. Using δ = i₁ + i₂ – A: 15 = 45 + i₂ – 30, so i₂ = 0°. Since the emergent angle is 0°, the ray is normal (perpendicular) to face AC. For refraction at face AB: r₁ + r₂ = A = 30°; since i₂ = 0°, r₂ = 0°, therefore r₁ = 30°. By Snell's law at face AB: n = sin i₁/sin r₁ = sin 45°/sin 30° = (1/√2)/(1/2) = 2/√2 = √2 ≈ 1.41.

Part (b)(i)(1): Slit separation d = 1.0 mm = 10⁻³ m (correcting from 'nm' which appears to be a misprint for 'mm'), D = 1.0 m. For third bright fringe (n=3), λ = 600 nm = 600 × 10⁻⁹ m: y = nλD/d = 3 × 600 × 10⁻⁹ × 1/(10⁻³) = 1.8 × 10⁻³ m = 1.8 mm.

Part (b)(i)(2): For bright fringes to coincide: n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂ → n₁ × 600 = n₂ × 480 → n₁/n₂ = 480/600 = 4/5. The minimum values are n₁ = 4 and n₂ = 5. Minimum distance = n₁λ₁D/d = 4 × 600 × 10⁻⁹ × 1/(10⁻³) = 2.4 × 10⁻³ m = 2.4 mm.

Part (b)(ii)(1): The intensity pattern for single slit diffraction shows a broad central maximum flanked by secondary maxima of rapidly decreasing intensity. The positions of zero intensity (minima) are given by: a sin θ = nλ, i.e., sin θ = nλ/a, where n = ±1, ±2, ±3, ... and a is the slit width. Part (b)(ii)(2): Diffraction of light differs from diffraction of sound in that light has a very small wavelength (400–700 nm) compared to everyday objects, so diffraction effects are only noticeable with very narrow slits or small obstacles. Sound waves have much larger wavelengths (centimetres to metres), comparable to everyday obstacles (doors, windows), so diffraction of sound is much more easily observed in daily life.

    (ii) किसी पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाले विद्युत फ्लक्स की परिभाषा लिखिए । गाउसीय पृष्ठ का महत्व दीजिए । किसी गाउसीय पृष्ठ के बाहर का आवेश उस पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाले कुल विद्युत फ्लक्स में कोई योगदान नहीं देता है । क्यों ?
    (iii) किसी लघु गोलीय खोल S₁ के भीतर बिन्दु आवेश q₁ = -3 μC, q₂ = -2 μC तथा q₃ = 9 μC हैं । यह खोल किसी अन्य बड़ी खोल S₂ में बन्द है । दोनों पृष्ठों S₁ और S₂ के बीच कोई आवेश Q स्थित है । यदि S₁ से गुजरने वाले विद्युत फ्लक्स की तुलना में S₂ से गुजरने वाला फ्लक्स 4 गुना है, तो आवेश Q ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A small conducting sphere A of radius r charged to a potential V, is enclosed by a spherical conducting shell B of radius R. If A and B are connected by a thin wire, calculate the final potential on sphere A and shell B.
    (ii) Write two characteristics of equipotential surfaces. A uniform electric field of 50 NC⁻¹ is set up in a region along +x axis. If the potential at the origin (0, 0) is 220 V, find the potential at a point (4m, 3m).
OR
(b) (i) What is difference between an open surface and a closed surface? Draw elementary surface vector dS→ for a spherical surface S.
    (ii) Define electric flux through a surface. Give the significance of a Gaussian surface. A charge outside a Gaussian surface does not contribute to total electric flux through the surface. Why?
    (iii) A small spherical shell S₁ has point charges q₁ = -3 μC, q₂ = -2 μC and q₃ = 9 μC inside it. This shell is enclosed by another big spherical shell S₂. A point charge Q is placed in between the two surfaces S₁ and S₂. If the electric flux through the surface S₂ is four times the flux through surface S₁, find charge Q.

key_points: 32(a)(i): When connected, charge redistributes; all charge moves to shell B; final potential = kQ_total/R = V_final = Vr/R on both A and B
32(a)(ii): Equipotential surfaces — no work done moving charge on them; E perpendicular to them. Potential at (4,3): V = 220 - E·Δx = 220 - 50×4 = 220-200 = 20 V
32(b)(iii): Flux through S₁ = (q₁+q₂+q₃)/ε₀ = 4μC/ε₀; Flux through S₂ = 4 × Flux(S₁) = 16μC/ε₀; total charge inside S₂ = 4 + Q; (4+Q)/ε₀ = 16μC/ε₀ so Q = 12 μC

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): The initial charge on sphere A is Q = 4πε₀rV (since V = kQ/r). When the thin wire connects A and B, charge redistributes. Since B is the outer shell and the system reaches equilibrium, all charge migrates to the outer shell B (as charge resides on the outermost surface). The final charge on shell B is Q and on sphere A is zero. The final potential of both A and B equals the potential due to all charges at radius R: V_final = kQ/R = (4πε₀rV)/(4πε₀R) = Vr/R. Both A and B attain the same final potential Vr/R.

Part (a)(ii): Two characteristics of equipotential surfaces: (1) No work is done in moving a charge along an equipotential surface. (2) The electric field is always perpendicular to the equipotential surface. For the potential calculation: The electric field E = 50 NC⁻¹ is along +x axis. Moving from origin to (4m, 3m), only displacement along x-axis matters (field is along x). Δx = 4 m, Δy = 3 m. Potential decreases in the direction of E: V(4,3) = V(0,0) – E × Δx = 220 – 50 × 4 = 220 – 200 = 20 V.

Part (b)(ii): Electric flux through a surface is defined as Φ = ∮E→·dS→, the surface integral of the electric field over the surface. The significance of a Gaussian surface is that it allows calculation of electric field for symmetric charge distributions using Gauss's law: Φ = q_enc/ε₀. A charge outside a Gaussian surface does not contribute to the net flux because the field lines entering the surface from outside also exit through it, so the net flux contribution from an external charge is zero (equal inward and outward flux).

Part (b)(iii): Net charge inside S₁ = q₁ + q₂ + q₃ = -3 + (-2) + 9 = +4 μC. Flux through S₁ = 4 μC/ε₀. Net charge inside S₂ = charge inside S₁ + Q = 4 + Q μC. Flux through S₂ = (4 + Q)/ε₀. Given: Flux(S₂) = 4 × Flux(S₁): (4 + Q)/ε₀ = 4 × (4/ε₀) = 16/ε₀. So 4 + Q = 16, giving Q = 12 μC.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) What is the source of force acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field? Obtain the expression for force acting between two long straight parallel conductors carrying steady currents and hence define 'ampere'.
    (ii) A point charge q is moving with velocity v→ in a uniform magnetic field B→. Find the work done by the magnetic force on the charge.
    (iii) Explain the necessary conditions in which the trajectory of a charged particle is helical in a uniform magnetic field.
OR
(b) (i) A current carrying loop can be considered as a magnetic dipole placed along its axis. Explain.
    (ii) Obtain the relation for magnetic dipole moment M→ of current carrying coil. Give the direction of M→.
    (iii) A current carrying coil is placed in an external uniform magnetic field. The coil is free to turn in the magnetic field. What is the net force acting on the coil? Obtain the orientation of the coil in stable equilibrium. Show that in this orientation the flux of the total field (field produced by the loop + external field) through the coil is maximum.

key_points: 33(a)(i): Source is interaction of magnetic field of current with external field; F/l = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); one ampere defined when F/l = 2×10⁻⁷ N/m
33(a)(ii): Magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity; work done = 0
33(a)(iii): Helical path when v has components both parallel and perpendicular to B; parallel component gives linear motion, perpendicular component gives circular motion
33(b)(ii): M = NIA; direction by right-hand rule (perpendicular to plane of coil)
33(b)(iii): Net force on coil in uniform field = 0; stable equilibrium when M→ parallel to B→; flux is maximum in this orientation

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): The source of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is the Lorentz force acting on the moving charge carriers (electrons) inside the conductor. For two parallel conductors separated by distance d, carrying currents I₁ and I₂: the magnetic field due to conductor 1 at conductor 2 is B₁ = μ₀I₁/(2πd). Force per unit length on conductor 2 is F/l = I₂B₁ = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd). One ampere is defined as that constant current which, when maintained in each of two infinitely long, straight, parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed 1 metre apart in vacuum, produces between them a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre of length.

Part (a)(ii): The magnetic force on a moving charge is F→ = q(v→ × B→), which is always perpendicular to the velocity v→. Since force is perpendicular to displacement at every instant, the work done by the magnetic force is zero (W = F→·ds→ = 0).

Part (a)(iii): For helical motion, the charged particle must have a velocity component parallel to the magnetic field (v_∥) and a velocity component perpendicular to it (v_⊥). The perpendicular component causes circular motion (centripetal force provided by magnetic force), while the parallel component is unaffected (no magnetic force along B→). The superposition of circular motion and uniform linear motion along B→ produces a helical trajectory.

Part (b)(i): A current-carrying loop produces a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet (magnetic dipole). The magnetic field lines emerge from one face (north pole) and enter the other face (south pole), exactly like a dipole. The field at large distances along the axis has the same dipole form as a magnetic dipole, justifying this analogy.

Part (b)(ii): For a current-carrying coil of N turns, area A, carrying current I, the magnetic dipole moment is M = NIA. The direction of M→ is perpendicular to the plane of the coil, given by the right-hand rule: curl the fingers in the direction of current flow; the thumb points in the direction of M→.

Part (b)(iii): In a uniform magnetic field, the net force on a current-carrying coil is zero because equal and opposite forces act on opposite sides of the coil, producing no net translational force. The torque on the coil is τ = M→ × B→. In stable equilibrium, τ = 0 and the system has minimum potential energy. This occurs when M→ is parallel to B→ (θ = 0°). In this orientation, the flux through the coil due to the total field (coil's own field + external field B) is maximum, since the coil's field and the external field are in the same direction inside the coil, adding up to give maximum total flux.
